title: Client-controlled price determines order total

trace.description: Protected JSON response or stored order; line references use fixed source

evidence.description: Alice POST /orders with book, quantity 1, unit_price_cents 1 returned 201 and total_cents 1; baseline price 1000 returned total 1000.

counterevidence: Pydantic bounds quantity to 1-5 and price to 1-100000; the SKU allowlist runs before insertion. These controls still permit a price of 1 for the 1000-cent book.

likelihood.reason: Any fixture member can send a single request with known IDs or price.

impact.reason: Defeats the documented boundary, but demonstrated consequences are limited to synthetic data or fake order accounting; no real financial loss or production exposure.

conditions.description: Valid member fixture token and access to the local application.

ext.remediation: Retain the accepted request schema but calculate every total from CATALOG[body.sku], including client overquotes.
ext.verification: python -m unittest app.test_security -v; python security-audit/reproduce.py. Matrices deny unauthorized reads, preserve authorized reads, and all five price variants use catalog totals.
